newsitem.title: USA: GM sued over anti-lock brake system.
newsitem.headline: GM sued over anti-lock brake system.

text.p: A class action lawsuit was filed on Wednesday against General Motors Corp and LucasVarity Plc alleging the defendants failed to correct a defective anti-lock brake system and did not warn customers about the problems.

The suit, filed in Manhattan federal court, seeks unspecified damages. The 10 plaintiffs, who sued on behalf of all owners of General Motors vehicles with the brake system, allege they made their purchases after reading advertisements and promotional materials that stressed quality and safety.
A spokesman for General Motors said the company had not yet seen the suit and could not comment.
The suit involves thousands of vehicles made by General Motors from 1989 through 1995 that are equipped with an anti-lock brake system (ABS) designed by Kelsey-Hayes Co, a unit of LucasVarity.
The suit alleges that GM and LucasVarity knew from at least 1990 that they were having severe difficulties with the quality and reliability of the ABS.
It alleges that the defendants were aware of defects in the design of the brake system, but never satisfactorily resolved these problems, or informed consumers about them.
The suit alleges that, during hard or emergency braking situations, the system is designed so the brake pedal will fall rapidly and without warning to the floor of the vehicle.
When this happens, the suit alleges that it appears to the driver that the brakes have failed completely leading to "foreseable panic reaction" that has caused and will continue to cause accidents.
The suit alleges that internal documents show that GM has acknowleged the "pedal to the floor" phenomenon, stating it gives the "perception" of the total loss of brakes.
